items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: You want to talk about what McCarthy did?

ctx.x: Yeah I think so. Yeah. Definitely. I’d have to say that probably “Excursion” is one of the things that — it’s not that I’m most proud of, because for instance like Hank and Billy, that record, I love the music on it, there are certain engineering values that I’m not too terribly excited about but forget their playing, they’re playing is always exemplary but it’s just the project and the way it came about and what happened as a result, I mean when I listened to it, it’s just a marvelous, Bill Mays, the two…

you know you hire people because of their individual voices and you put them together not because you want them to make a sound that you think they should make but because you hear what they do and you want to put them together with the individual voices so that they will interact and make whatever sound comes out of that. And that’s what Miles did. Miles would always do that. Miles was not a person that said I want you to sound like this, I want you to play like this. If anything Miles said, “Uh, you’re not…
